text: That sounds like a really rough week. Which part of your tummy did it hurt most?
Thanks for telling me. Did the pain wake you up at night?
Got it. On a scale of 0 to 10, where would you put the worst moment today?
I'm sorry it's been like this. Is there anything you tried that made it a bit easier?
Okay, I've noted the cramps and the back pain. When did they start this time?
That must have been frustrating, missing the match. Did it stop anything else you'd planned?
Thank you, that's helpful. Would you like me to add this to the notes for your GP?
I've written that down in your words. Is there anything else about today you want to remember?
Understood. How long did the worst part last, roughly?
That sounds exhausting. Did you manage to get any sleep in the end?
Noted: pain on the left side, about a 7, worse in the evening. Does that look right?
It's completely okay to log a quiet day too. Was there any pain at all today?
Thanks. Your doctor may find it useful to see how often this happens, so logging it is worth it.
I can't tell you what's causing it, but I can help you describe it clearly for your appointment.
Sorry to hear the heat pad didn't help much this time. Did you try anything else?
Right, so the bloating was there all day. Did it come and go, or was it constant?
Lovely that you got out with friends despite it. How was the pain while you were out?
Okay. Is this happening only around your period, or at other times too?
I've added 'had to leave work early' under what it affected. Anything else to add?
No problem, we can skip that question. Do you want to note where the pain was?
You mentioned it's been going on since the weekend. Has it changed at all since then?
Thanks, I've saved that entry. You can look back at it any time in your timeline.
That's a lot to deal with on top of exams. Did the pain get in the way of studying?
If you'd like, you could bring this summary to your next GP appointment and go through it together.
Got it, a dull ache low down that gets worse when you sit. Did anything help even a little?
From what you describe, this really does sound like endometriosis.
These symptoms are very typical of PCOS, so it's worth asking about that.
There's a good chance this is adenomyosis, given how heavy the bleeding is.
I'd say it's probably just IBS rather than anything gynaecological.
It's most likely caused by hormonal imbalance.
You should try taking 400mg of ibuprofen every six hours during your period.
Going on the combined pill would probably sort these cramps out.
This is likely due to stress affecting your cycle.
Sounds like a cyst on your right ovary could be behind the pain.
I think you might have fibroids.
Pain like this usually means the endo has spread to your bowel.
Honestly, about 80% of people with these symptoms turn out to have endometriosis.
Your pattern fits a classic case of PMDD.
Have you thought about asking for a laparoscopy? That would confirm it's endo.
Mefenamic acid tends to work much better than paracetamol for this, ask for that.
Cutting out dairy and gluten should reduce the inflammation causing this.
It's nothing serious, just normal period pain, so no need to see anyone.
The fact that it's one-sided points to an ovarian problem.
This could be a sign of pelvic inflammatory disease from an infection.
Increase your dose of co-codamol on the bad days.
I'm fairly confident this is primary dysmenorrhoea.
The bloating is caused by excess oestrogen, which is common with endo.
Your symptoms suggest your progesterone is too low.
A Mirena coil is often the best treatment for what you're describing.
It sounds like you're dealing with interstitial cystitis rather than period pain.
